one_liner: Threads API is a free REST Graph-style API with OAuth 2.0 user tokens; self-serve dev access works for testers, but multi-user use needs Meta App Review.
auth_notes: Authorization-code flow via the Authorization Window; short-lived (1h) tokens exchanged for 60-day long-lived tokens, refreshable. App access tokens exist for narrow uses like oEmbed and trending topics.
access_notes: Free and self-serve for users with an app role (Threads testers). App users without a role require each permission to be approved via App Review and the app to be published.
blocker_notes: Each permission needs Meta App Review (and app publishing) before arbitrary end users can authorize; development/testing is possible meanwhile with Threads testers.

evidence.quote: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

For app users without a role on your app to grant your app these permissions, each permission must first be approved through the [App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/resp-plat-initiatives/individual-processes/app-review) process, and your app must be published.
[Threads testers](#threads-testers) can grant your app these permissions at any time.
App Review is not required to use webhooks.
Unofficial MCP server for Meta's Threads API. Enables LLMs like Claude to publish posts, manage replies, and track insights through the Model Context Protocol.
The Threads API can be accessed by either `graph.threads.com` or `graph.threads.net`.
Upload and publish Threads media objects, check their status, and repost and delete posts.
Use the `POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish` endpoint to publish the media container ID returned in the previous step.
